key_insight: TASK memory reduces hallucinations even when the correct memory is already retrieved by controlling whether an LLM applies external memory or relies on its parametric knowledge.
engineering_relevance: Memory-backed agents may need query-dependent control inside the model, not just better retrieval, to handle updated facts without misapplying them to unrelated entities.
method: Store factual content in an external text note.
Use a removable knowledge edit to provide a shared in-model address and support multi-hop composition.
Apply two content-free steering vectors to control memory adoption query by query.
evidence_signal: Across five open models under a pre-registered, test-once protocol, TASK reduced memory-ignoring hallucinations to at most 1.5% in all ten model–dataset cells, with 21 of 23 cross-model comparisons statistically significant.
watch_item: Deployment requires internal activation access and removable weight edits; the abstract does not establish reliability beyond the tested 8B–27B open models and memory libraries of up to 3,000 entries.
paper_title: TASK Memory: Beyond Text-Only Memory with Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing against Memory Hallucination
